# Financial Sector Update

Report 068 | Published 2021-10-03 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2021-10-3/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/068.json)

Inflation persistence, crypto governance, and discounted banks.

Persistent inflation and rent pressure were useful calls. Sberbank exposed the difference between cheap fundamentals and investable foreign-holder rights; DBS and CNQ fared well. Treasury-heavy bank portfolios were incorrectly treated as broadly safe. Crypto analysis correctly identified correlation and legal distinctions, but sometimes converted complex securities, governance and tax questions into overly categorical claims.

**Coverage:** Read all blocks 0-199 and image labels. Material epidemiology, inflation, currency, yield, uranium, crypto/legal, bank and valuation theses included. Anecdotes are not promoted into representative statistics; routine holdings and incidental levels excluded.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [MOVe-OUT full results](https://www.merck.com/news/merck-and-ridgeback-biotherapeutics-provide-update-on-results-from-move-out-study-of-molnupiravir-an-investigational-oral-antiviral-medicine-in-at-risk-adults-with-mild-to-moderate-covid-19/) | Merck | 2021-11-26 | Verified in the audit

Interim relative risk reduction 48%, with enrollment stopped on monitoring committee recommendation; full analysis reduction 30%, events 6.8% versus 9.7%. Interim result was real, not final efficacy.

### 068-C12

**Benefits no employment**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | empirical |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | unemployment-benefits |
| Source blocks | 54 |
| Thesis family | unemployment-benefits |

The endorsed no-increase interpretation is too strong. Recipient-level study finds employment rose 6.8 percentage points after early withdrawal, while benefit loss was much larger than earnings recovery. A shortage can persist despite a positive effect.

**Direction:** Contradicted for the defined proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Early withdrawal of pandemic unemployment insurance](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/pandp.20221009) | Coombs et al, AEA Papers and Proceedings | 2022-05-01 | Verified in the audit

Bank-transaction difference-in-differences study of 16,253 recipients: benefit receipt declined 36.3 percentage points, employment rose 6.8 pp by early September; cumulative benefits fell $2,529, earnings rose $292. Ending aid did increase employment but did not replace lost income broadly.

### 068-C13

**Old CPI doubled**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Evidence needed |
| Type | empirical |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | inflation-measurement |

| Thesis family | inflation-measurement |

The low-double-digit assertion has no reproducible old-method index here. BLS documentation undermines treating methodology as a fixed large add-on, but does not by itself calculate October 2021 under old housing rules.

**Direction:** Not resolved by collected evidence.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Next test:** Reconstruct 1980 housing/interest-cost weights and formulas using 2021 data; do not substitute an unexplained constant adjustment.

**Outcome evidence:**

- [CPI misconceptions](https://www.bls.gov/cpi/factsheets/common-misconceptions-about-cpi.htm) | BLS | Verified in the audit

BLS rejects large constant adjustments attributed to methodological changes. Geometric means reduced annual growth less than 0.3 percentage points; the pre-1983 housing asset approach can yield lower inflation when housing prices fall. No 2021 old-method reconstruction is provided.
